desc: రొయ్యల ఇగురు. Royyala iguru, the coastal Andhra prawn roast: prawns cooked down in onion masala with hill turmeric powder and fiery Teja chilli powder. Serves 4.

ingredients: ½ tsp hill turmeric powder · 1½ tsp Teja chilli powder
1 tsp coriander powder · ½ tsp garam masala
steps: Rub the prawns with half the turmeric and a little salt; set aside 10 minutes.
Fry the onions in the oil till golden, then the ginger-garlic paste till it smells cooked.
Add the rest of the turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute.
Add the prawns and cook till they curl and turn pink, 5–6 minutes. Finish with garam masala.
approved.meta: Teja is very hot · use 1 tsp for medium heat.

intro: Iguru is the Andhra way of cooking meat or prawns down in a thick onion masala until almost dry, so the spices cling to every piece. Royyala iguru comes from the coastal districts, from Nellore to Godavari to Srikakulam, where prawns from the backwaters and the sea are a Sunday lunch with rice.
Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) goes on the prawns first and into the masala. Teja chilli powder brings the deep red colour and strong heat coastal homes like, so scale it to your table.
quick: Rub prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onions and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala till it coats them.

time_note: Prep includes cleaning the prawns and the 10-minute rest with turmeric.
groups: medium size, shelled and deveined, weighed after cleaning
Konda Pasupu; ¼ tsp for the prawns, ¼ tsp for the masala
very hot; use 1 tsp for medium heat, ½ tsp for mild
steps: Shell and devein the prawns, rinse them well and drain in a colander.
Rub the prawns with half the turmeric and a little salt; set aside 10 minutes. Use ¼ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp of the salt.
Heat the oil in a heavy kadai on medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the green chillies and curry leaves.
Fry the onions in the oil till golden, then the ginger-garlic paste till it smells cooked. The onions take about 8–10 minutes; the paste about 1 minute, until the raw smell goes.
If using the tomato, add it now and cook until soft and pulpy, about 4 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Add the rest of the turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute. Add the remaining salt and stir so the spices do not catch.
Pour in the water and cook the masala on medium heat until the oil starts to separate at the edges, about 3–4 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook till they curl and turn pink, 5–6 minutes. Finish with garam masala. Stir often on medium-high heat so the masala dries and coats the prawns.
Check doneness: prawns are cooked when they are pink and opaque all the way through and curled into a loose C. Cut one open if unsure; there should be no grey, see-through centre.
Taste for salt, scatter the coriander leaves and switch off. Do not keep cooking once the prawns are done, or they turn rubbery.
tips: Teja is very hot: 1½ tsp makes a fiery iguru the way coastal homes like it; use 1 tsp for medium heat, or ½ tsp for mild.
Fry the onions until properly golden; the colour and body of an iguru come from well-browned onions.
Prawns cook fast. A loose C shape means done; a tight O means overcooked and chewy.
Pat the prawns dry after rinsing so they fry in the masala instead of stewing in water.
variations: Gongura royyalu: stir in ½ cup gongura leaves, wilted in a little oil and mashed, with the prawns.
Coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut or 3 tbsp thick coconut milk in the last 2 minutes for a softer, richer masala.
Gravy style: add ¾ cup water after the prawns for a thinner royyala kura to pour over rice.
serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with rasam or sambar rice. It also goes well with chapati.
storage: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Reheat in a pan only until steaming hot all the way through; longer reheating makes the prawns tough.
faq: How do I know when prawns are cooked?
They turn pink and opaque all the way through and curl into a loose C shape, usually in 5–6 minutes in the hot masala. A grey, see-through centre means they need a little longer.
What is the difference between iguru and vepudu?

Iguru is cooked down in an onion masala until thick and almost dry, with the masala clinging to the prawns. Vepudu is a fry, with less or no onion gravy, cooked until the prawns are crisp at the edges.
How can I make royyala iguru less spicy?
Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder for medium heat or ½ tsp for mild, and skip the green chillies. A tablespoon of curd or coconut milk at the end also softens the heat.
